replace_all.description: write_db with db_op 'str_replace' only: replace every occurrence of old_str in the field instead of requiring it to occur exactly once (default false). old_str must still occur at least once.

if_version.description: write_db with db_op 'set', 'update', 'str_replace' or 'delete' (a 'batch' pins each entry in `writes` instead): the document's `version` as you last read it (every read_db document carries it, and so does every set, update and str_replace result). Pass it on every write to a document you have read: the write applies only if the document is still at that version; otherwise nothing is written and the result names the current version — so pin the write instead of re-reading first to check. Optional; omit it only for a document you have not read.

as_level.description: read_db and write_db only: act at this access level instead of your own — 'interact' is any signed-in viewer who can use the page, 'admin' a co-owner — to check what the page's access rules let such a user do. It narrows, never raises, your access; the call still reads and writes your own data/users subtree. At a lowered level a write the rules refuse reads as not found and a refused read as empty. Omit it to act as yourself.

query.description: Options for db_op 'list' and 'query': `limit` and `cursor` (from a prior result's `next_cursor`) page through a collection; `where` clauses ([field, operator, value] triples) and `order_by` filter and order a 'query' only.

data.description: write_db: document fields to write, as a JSON object — db_op 'set' (replaces the document) and 'update' (merges into it) take exactly one of `data` or `file_path`; not accepted with any other db_op.

file_path.description: Path to the .html file to render — or, for an Artifact created from an Artifact type, one of its own data files. Required to publish (the default action), except with `type_url`. Use a short, distinctive basename — it is the last-resort title when the HTML has no <title> and no `title` parameter is given. For 'upload_asset', the local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet (CSS), script (JS), or text (CSV, Markdown, JSON, plain text) file to upload. For 'write_db' (db_op 'set' or 'update'), a local JSON file whose top-level object is sent as the document — an alternative to inline `data`, so a large document need not pass through the conversation.

favicon.description: The artifact's emoji: one or two emoji (e.g. "📊"). No markup. Required on a page's first publish; omit on a redeploy (same file path this session, or `url`) to keep the artifact's emoji — pass a new one only when the user asks. Optional for data files on an Artifact created from an Artifact type and with `type_url` (the type's emoji stays unless you pass one with files).

icon.description: Optional. One short generic word for the artifact's tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map — a plain signifier, not a product or brand name. Omit when republishing to keep the current icon. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page. Map form {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null} publishes each source at the key (what the HTML references) — an {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file server side (an Artifact you can open, same organization; its type comes with it; not an HTML, SVG or XML document; at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish); when updating an existing artifact, files left out of the map are kept and null removes that path. List form publishes each file at its own spelling. Local sources must lie under the working directory or your scratchpad directory (as your system prompt names it). `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved — it runs against open pages when you publish updates; it must be a ≤ 8 KiB ES module whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact and it must be in your organization.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: Base directory that relative SOURCE paths resolve against (like a bundler root) — saves retyping a long build prefix. Never changes published paths. Relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or your scratchpad directory (so files fetched or built there publish without copying). Requires `files` — except for an Artifact made from an Artifact type (or being created from one), where it may stand alone and a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

limit.description: list only: maximum artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list only: 'mine' (default) lists artifacts the user owns — the only ones the update flow can target; 'shared' lists artifacts other people shared with the user (read-only); 'all' lists both. Rows are labeled (mine)/(shared) whenever scope is not 'mine'. With `type` or `type_url` (the Artifacts made from a type) the default is 'all': the user's own and the ones shared across their organization.

title.description: Title for the artifact — the name shown in the browser tab and gallery. A short, distinctive noun-phrase name — not a generic label, a summary, or a name with an appended explainer. Prefer a <title> tag at the top of the HTML itself; this parameter fills in only when the file lacks one in the first 8KB of the file, and never overrides the tag. HTML publishes only — Markdown pages keep their filename identity. Content always comes from file_path — there is no inline content parameter. On a `type_url` create there is no HTML file and none of that applies: `title` is simply the new Artifact's name — what the user called it, or a short descriptive name; left out, it is named after the type (e.g. just "Slides").

description.description: One-sentence subtitle shown on the gallery card. Say what the page is or does.

label.description: A short name for this publish, max 60 chars (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional — a few words, not a description.

url.description: Existing artifact URL to update in place. Pass whenever the user wants to update an artifact this conversation did not publish — "update my artifact", "keep the same link", a pasted artifact URL — and find the URL with action: "list" or ask the user for the link if you don't have it; without this, the publish creates a separate artifact instead of updating the existing one. Omit for new artifacts and same-conversation redeploys. Must be an artifact the user owns. For 'read' and the other url-addressed actions: the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: URL of an Artifact type to create this Artifact from (people may call a type a template or a starter). The new Artifact starts as a private copy of the type's current release, and `file_path`/`files` become its own files alongside the type's (omit them to create it without files of its own). Always creates a new Artifact — omit `url`; update it afterwards by its `url` like any other. The type's files, its page included, can't be replaced on it. With action "describe_type": the type to describe (a link from a list_types result); with action "list": the type whose Artifacts to list (or name it with `type` instead).

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the user. Pass "after_first_write" when you will fill it right after creating it (a later "write_db", or a files publish to its url), so the user does not first see it empty — it then opens on that first write. Omit otherwise: it opens when created.

prompt.description: read only: what to extract from an artifact shared with the user — its content reaches you as an isolated summary answering this. Ignored for artifacts the user owns and for a page published in this session's own Slack channel (raw content is returned); optional.

force.description: Last-resort overwrite that DISCARDS the newer published version's page — another session's publish, or someone's save from a page that can publish new versions of itself. Its supporting files are not discarded: every published file stays unless this publish replaces it or removes it with a null `files` entry (action "list_files" shows what is published). On a conflict the fix is to merge your changes onto the newer content (handed to you in the rejection, or re-read) and publish again — not force. Pass force:true only when the user has explicitly said to discard that specific version; never to get past a conflict on your own judgment. The tracked baseVersion is still sent; with force:true the server treats it as informational and overwrites, unless it refuses force over a version saved from inside the page. Omit (or false) so a concurrent write conflicts instead of being silently clobbered.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the user's claude.ai sidebar once it is published — pass it only when the user asked for that; a pin that fails never fails the publish (the result says so).

thread_id.description: reply: id of the comment thread to reply into. resolve: the thread to mark resolved. comments: read just this one thread (the size cap can still elide a very long thread). Thread ids come from action "comments" and from comment notifications.

text.description: reply only: the reply text. Plain text, at most 4096 bytes of UTF-8.

cursor.description: comments only: continue a listing that ended with a "more threads not listed" line — pass the cursor value that line names to render the threads it could not fit.

acknowledge_duplicate.description: reply only: post even though a Claude reply already stands after every "sent to Claude" request on the thread. Without it such a reply is refused as a likely duplicate. Pass true only for a deliberate follow-up that adds something new — never to restate what the standing reply said.

out_dir.description: read_asset: directory to save the file into (default: the working directory); the file is named by the asset id plus the extension for its type. read_file: directory to save under — default: this artifact’s folder in your scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval and which you can Read from; any other directory asks the user before each save. tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. content.content: @AGENTS.md

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Style Guide

### UI Guidelines

- Use Tailwind CSS for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use tailwind classes
- Use platform-native UI components (see below) first with shadcn/ui as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles

content.text:
CI is green and the PR is still `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`. Here's where it stands.

## Fixed and pushed (commit `ENG-2189 Address bot review findings…`)

**Bots**
- **CodeRabbit** — `canvasNodeShortcuts` had no `data-setting-id`. Added `settingAnchor([PERSONAL_KEYS.canvasNodeShortcuts])` on the grid wrapper. Valid, resolved.
- **Codex P1 (CSS)** — valid: `--dg-neutral-dark` / `--dg-border` are defined nowhere in the repo, so only the fallback hexes ever painted. Heading now uses the Blueprint palette with a `.bp3-dark` override, matching the pattern already in [styles.css](apps/roam/src/styles/styles.css:193). Left the thread open since Michael tagged you on it.
- **Codex P2 (trigger placeholder)** — declined the suggested fix: the personal override is an `IKeyCombo`, the graph-wide `trigger` is a trigger character, so showing one as the other's placeholder would mislead. But the blankness it spotted was real, so I reverted the `placeholder=""` and the `placeholder` prop that existed only to pass it — the field shows "Click to set trigger" again, as before this PR. Resolved with that explanation.

**Michael — the ones with an obvious code action** (replied, left unresolved for him)
- `resolveSettingsTabId` — moved the default into the parameter as he asked; `id` is undefined when the plain "Open settings" command opens the dialog with no target tab.
- `useLegacyConfigBlocks` stale-default comment — he's right. ENG-2173 is on `main` but not in this stack's base, so the comment named a default that no longer holds. Reworded to not name one.
- The terse `LegacyConfigBlock` comment ("?") — reworded to say it mirrors the block-sync props the BlockPropSettingPanels take.

Roam typecheck, lint (no new warnings on changed lines), and 142 unit tests pass. The dark-mode heading was not visually verified in a live Roam — it's a color swap plus a new `.bp3-dark` rule, and light-mode behaviour is unchanged.

## Needs you — these are yours to answer

1. **Feature-gated tab hiding** ([Settings.tsx:172](apps/roam/src/components/settings/Settings.tsx:172) + [LeftSidebarSettings.tsx:32](apps/roam/src/components/settings/LeftSidebarSettings.tsx:32)). Michael wants the hide-when-disabled behaviour kept, and flags that a non-admin hitting a blank tab is poor UX once "Enable left sidebar" is admin-gated. He also says he's unsure whether you two re-clarified where feature flags should live. This is the one real design conflict — the tab can't both host the enabling toggle and hide itself, so it needs a decision (move the flag back out to a preferences tab, or accept the always-visible tab).

2. **"Why are we not using tailwind?"** (settingsStyles.css 24 and 34, plus "Roam ships no Tailwind preflight?" on 23). Partly answered in code — the group wrapper is now plain `flex flex-col gap-1` and the dead `dg-settings-group__rows` class is gone. The heading rule stays hand-rolled because `border-b-2` sets only a width; without preflight there's no `border-style`/color default, so it paints nothing. Worth confirming he's happy with that split before I reply on his behalf.

3. **`grid-cols-[auto_auto]` in Roam.** Pre-existing — it came in with #952, not this PR. Roam ships its own compiled Tailwind, so an arbitrary-value class is almost certainly absent and the grid is falling back to a single implicit column. Your call whether to fix it here (out of scope) or file it.

4. **"Can you give an example of a saved deep link?"** ([settingsTabs.ts:19](apps/roam/src/components/settings/utils/settingsTabs.ts:19)) — his skepticism is justified. Nothing parses a tab id out of a URL; the only callers are three in-repo ones, all already updated. So the alias map protects external/stored callers of the exported dialog, not user-saved links. Either the comment should be reworded or the map dropped — I didn't want to delete it unilaterally.

5. **"Can you give an example of this?"** on the `blockKey` comment ([BlockPropSettingPanels.tsx:38](apps/roam/src/components/settings/components/BlockPropSettingPanels.tsx:38)) — concrete answer available: `Canvas Page Format` and `(BETA) Left Sidebar` in `useLegacyConfigBlocks`, whose titles in the UI differ from the block text `discourseConfigRef` matches on. Say the word and I'll post it.

6. FYI only, no action: he noted the discourse context overlay is being removed in ENG-2096.

content.text:
Answers to each, in order.

## 2. Tailwind — tested, and it works (already pushed)

Roam serves `assets/css/tailwind.min.css`, a **pre-JIT Tailwind 2 build (~6550 rules)**. I loaded it in the browser and read computed styles off real elements. Three facts:

| class | computed | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `font-semibold` | `600` | works |
| `text-base` / `text-lg` | `14px` / `15.75px` | works, but Roam's root font-size is **14px**, so `1rem ≠ 16px` |
| `border-b-2` | **`0px none`** | paints nothing |
| `grid-cols-[auto_auto]` | `none` | **doesn't exist** |

My original comment was right in substance but named the wrong mechanism, which is why it read as hand-waving. The real reason: `border-b-2` sets *only* `border-bottom-width`. Tailwind's preflight normally supplies `border-style: solid; border-width: 0` for every element — Roam doesn't ship preflight, so with no border-style the browser computes the used width as 0. The fix is `border-0 border-b-2 border-solid`. (Plain `border-solid` without `border-0` is a trap: every other side then inherits the browser's `medium` = 3px.)

So the heading is now Tailwind, and the CSS file holds only what Tailwind can't express — the two colors, because dark mode needs a `.bp3-dark` selector:

```
"text-lg font-semibold leading-tight pb-2 border-0 border-b-2 border-solid dg-settings-heading"
```

Verified against Roam's actual stylesheet: 15.75px / 600, 2px solid rule in both themes, no stray top border. One deliberate change: the heading is 15.75px instead of 16px, since `text-lg` is the nearest step. Rows are 14px, so it still outranks them.

## 3. The `grid-cols-[auto_auto]` comment

[Michael's comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1373#discussion_r3985273833) on [CanvasShortcutSettings.tsx:106](apps/roam/src/components/settings/CanvasShortcutSettings.tsx:106) — he asked "Is `grid-cols-[auto_auto]` recognized in roam?"

Answer: **no.** Roam's Tailwind predates JIT, so it contains **zero** arbitrary-value rules. `grid-template-columns` computes to `none` — the "two-column" shortcut grid has been falling back to one implicit column since #952 shipped it. Not introduced here; the line only appears in the diff because the file moved.

It's not isolated — 9 call sites in apps/roam use arbitrary values and all are inert:

- `text-[#5c7080]`, `bg-[#f7f9fc]`, `border-[#d3d8de]`, `text-[13px]` (DiscourseNodeMenu, CanvasEmbedDialog, RelationTypeDropdown)
- `min-w-[160px]`, `max-h-[240px]` (PageGroupPanel, RelationTypeDropdown)
- `font-[inherit] text-[inherit]` (DiscourseRelationConfigPanel)

Worth its own ticket. Want me to draft one?

## 5. `resolveSettingsTabId` — Michael's premise is half right

He's right that we never pass an *unknown* id. He's wrong that the id is always known: **two entry points pass nothing at all**.

- [registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts:344](apps/roam/src/utils/registerCommandPaletteCommands.ts:344) — `renderSettings({ onloadArgs })`, the plain "open settings" command
- [DiscourseFloatingMenu.tsx:71](apps/roam/src/components/DiscourseFloatingMenu.tsx:71) — same

`selectedTabId` is optional on `SettingsDialog` precisely so those two can say "just open it". So `undefined` is a real, reachable case — and his suggested fix (default in the parameter) is the right shape for it, which is what I pushed.

The separate line-32 comment ("unknown ids pass through") is the weak one. Per-node tabs don't exist in this dialog — `DiscourseNodeConfigPanel` is nested *inside* the Nodes tab. Nothing passes a uid-keyed tab id. I'd delete that comment; the passthrough is just the `??` fallback, not a documented contract.

## 4. "Saved deep link" — he's right, the term is wrong

There is no URL-level deep link. Nothing anywhere parses a tab id out of a hash or query string. The only callers of `selectedTabId` are three in-repo ones, all already updated in this PR.

So nothing "saves" one. `SETTINGS_TAB_ALIASES` is defensive coverage for callers outside the repo — `SettingsDialog` is exported, and a user script or another extension could pass an old id. That's a much weaker justification than the comment implies. Two honest options: reword to say exactly that, or drop the alias map. I'd keep the map (it's 9 lines and protects against silent wrong-tab landings) and rewrite the comment. Your call.

## ENG-2173 — comment only, the code is fine

Nothing to fix behaviorally. ENG-2173 (`8a6d5379f`, on `main`) doesn't change the schema default — `zodSchema.ts` still says `.default(false)`. It added `migratePropsStoreDefault.ts`, which at startup writes `Use new settings store: true` into the graph's feature-flag block props. And `bulkReadSettings` still falls back to `readAllLegacyPersonalSettings()` for any user whose personal migration marker isn't set.

So the legacy config tree that `useLegacyConfigBlocks` writes to is still read, and the dual-write is still correct. What changed is only the *framing*: `false` is no longer what a real graph runs with. My comment asserted it was "the default", which is why he flagged it. Reworded, no code change needed.

Also worth knowing: **ENG-2173 is not in this stack's base.** `roam-setting-overhaul` branched before it, so it arrives at merge time. Nothing here conflicts with it.

## 1. Feature-gated tab hiding — the options

You said keep it. The constraint that forced it out is: *a tab that hides itself cannot host the control that un-hides it.* So the question is only where the "Enable left sidebar" toggle goes. Four shapes:

**A. Toggle back to Preferences → General; tab hidden when off.** Restores the pre-PR arrangement: `hidden={!leftSidebarEnabled}` on the tab, plus the `visibleTabId` guard that bounces the selection to a safe tab. Closest to the original scoping and to what Michael asked for. Cost: the toggle sits two tabs away from everything it controls, which is the wart the taxonomy was meant to remove. Also the command-palette entry that deep-links to the Left sidebar tab needs to handle the tab being hidden.

**B. Toggle to the Admin panel, with the other feature flags.** `Suggestive mode overlay`, `Advanced node search`, `Node sharing`, `Use new settings store` already live there. This is the cleanest answer to Michael's actual open question ("where should feature flags live") and it pre-answers the admin-gating he expects. Cost: a non-admin can't turn the left sidebar on at all any more — that may be exactly the intent, or a behavior change that needs its own decision.

**C. Toggle stays on the Left sidebar tab; tab hidden when off (current PR + hiding).** Internally contradictory — once you turn it off, you can't turn it back on. Not viable, listed only to rule it out.

**D. Tab always visible, but an empty state instead of blank.** "Left sidebar is disabled — enable it in Preferences → General." Fixes the blank-screen UX Michael flagged without hiding anything. Doesn't satisfy "keep the hiding", so it's a complement to A or B, not a substitute.

My read: **B, with D's empty state as a safety net if a deep link lands someone on a hidden tab.** It answers the flag-location question once rather than per-feature, and it matches where the admin gating is going anyway. But B changes who can enable the feature, so it's a product call — and Michael explicitly said he's unsure whether you two re-clarified the scoping. That's the one to settle with him directly.

---

CI is green on both pushes. I haven't replied on GitHub about the Tailwind findings or the deep-link wording yet — say the word and I'll post them.

content.text:
Two different things were packed into that phrase, and only one of them is the real constraint. Let me separate them.

**What "predates JIT" means.** Arbitrary values — the `[...]` bracket syntax like `grid-cols-[auto_auto]` or `text-[13px]` — aren't a CSS feature, they're a *compiler* feature. Classic Tailwind generated a fixed catalog of utilities from your config ahead of time; a class had to be in that catalog or it didn't exist. There was no mechanism to invent `w-[762px]` on demand, because nothing was reading your markup at build time. The JIT engine changed that: it scans your source files and generates a rule for whatever it finds, including bracket syntax. JIT shipped as opt-in in Tailwind 2.1 and became the only engine in v3.

Roam's `tailwind.min.css` is a pre-generated v2-era file. I confirmed the era from what's in and out of it: `backdrop-blur-sm` is there (v2.x), `snap-center` and `break-inside-avoid` are not (both v3 additions). And the decisive check — **zero selectors in all 6550 rules contain a bracket**. So the brackets aren't failing to match; those rules were never generated.

**The correction worth making.** I implied our classes work by coincidence of Roam happening to use them. That's wrong, and I checked rather than leave it standing. I probed utilities no human writes by hand — `gap-72`, `skew-y-12`, `col-start-7`, `place-content-evenly`, `divide-y-reverse` — and every one is present. That's a **full, unpurged build**: the entire v2 default catalog, not a subset purged down to Roam's own markup.

That's a much better situation than "coincidence." The practical rule for apps/roam is:

- Any standard Tailwind 2 utility works — you're not limited to what Roam itself uses.
- Arbitrary `[...]` values never work. Use a CSS rule.
- v3-era utilities never work (scroll snap, `break-inside-*`, the v3 color additions).
- Preflight is separately absent, which is why `border-b-2` needs `border-0 border-solid` — that's an unrelated gap from the JIT question.
- `1rem` is 14px here, so `text-base` is 14px, not 16px.

I've saved this to memory so it doesn't need re-deriving. The reproduction is cheap if you ever want to confirm: open roamresearch.com, append an element with the classes, read `getComputedStyle`.

content.text:
No. In every one of the nine cases the arbitrary class produces *nothing* — so whatever the motivation, the mechanism was never right. But the wants behind them split into three groups, and they're not equally defensible.

**Colors — six of the nine sites, and the least defensible.** `text-[#5c7080]`, `border-[#d3d8de]`, `hover:bg-[#f7f9fc]`, `bg-[#333]`, `hover:bg-[#f0f0f0]`. These are Blueprint palette hexes; `#5c7080` is Blueprint's gray1. The want is real — Tailwind's gray ramp doesn't contain them (`gray-500` is `#6b7280`, a different hue), so no catalog class hits those values. But apps/roam/AGENTS.md already says not to introduce arbitrary colors and to reach for Blueprint or Roam-native styling instead, which is the actual answer here. Worth noting: these elements are currently rendering with inherited defaults and nobody has filed a bug, which suggests the exact hexes weren't load-bearing to begin with.

**Genuine catalog gaps — two sites.** `min-w-[160px]`: Tailwind 2 ships only `min-w-0 / full / min / max`, no scale values, so there is no catalog class for this. `font-[inherit] text-[inherit]`: v2 has no `inherit` utilities at all. Both of these really do need a CSS rule — there was never a Tailwind way to write them in this build.

**Had a catalog option — the rest.** `max-h-[240px]` could be `max-h-60` (15rem, 210px at Roam's 14px root — not identical, but a scale value). `text-[13px]` is near `text-sm`. `grid-cols-[auto_auto]` is the interesting one: `grid-cols-2` exists but means two equal fractions, whereas `auto auto` means size-to-content. Different intent — and for a label/control pair, a flex row is the better fix anyway.

**Why it happened.** Bracket syntax is muscle memory from Tailwind 3, and nothing in this app pushes back. apps/roam has no Tailwind build — `tailwind.config.ts` is literally commented "required for editor support" with `content: []`. So there's no compiler to reject the class, no purge step, no lint rule. The string lands in the DOM and silently does nothing. Editor tooling makes it *worse*, since your IDE autocompletes against a Tailwind 3 config that doesn't describe what Roam serves.

That's the part worth fixing structurally rather than site by site: an ESLint rule banning bracket classes in apps/roam would catch this at review time and cost nothing ongoing — CI already surfaces new lint findings on changed lines. Want me to fold that into the ticket for the nine sites?

input.args:
Title: Remove inert arbitrary-value Tailwind classes from apps/roam and add a lint rule

Context: apps/roam builds no CSS of its own — Tailwind classes resolve against Roam's own prebuilt assets/css/tailwind.min.css, which is a pre-JIT Tailwind 2 build (~6550 rules). Verified in-browser: zero selectors in that sheet contain a bracket, so every arbitrary-value class (the `[...]` syntax) is inert. It is a full unpurged build, so all standard v2 utilities do work; only arbitrary values and v3-era utilities are missing. Tailwind's preflight is also absent, so `border-b-2` needs `border-0 border-b-2 border-solid` to paint.

Nine inert call sites in apps/roam/src:
- components/DiscourseNodeMenu.tsx:382 — border-[#d3d8de], hover:border-[#bfccd6], hover:bg-[#f7f9fc]
- components/settings/DiscourseRelationConfigPanel.tsx:1130 — font-[inherit], text-[inherit]
- components/settings/PageGroupPanel.tsx:184 — min-w-[160px]
- components/canvas/CanvasEmbedDialog.tsx:37 and :41 — text-[#5c7080]
- components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:84 — max-h-[240px], min-w-[160px]
- components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:92 — text-[13px], text-[#333], hover:bg-[#f0f0f0]
- components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:106 — bg-[#333]
(A tenth, grid-cols-[auto_auto] in CanvasShortcutSettings.tsx, was already removed in PR 1373.)

Scope: replace each with a catalog utility where one exists; for the genuine v2 gaps (min-w at a px value, font/text inherit) use a CSS rule. The hex colors are Blueprint palette values — apps/roam/AGENTS.md already says to use Blueprint or Roam-native styling rather than arbitrary colors, so prefer that over recreating the hex. Then add an ESLint rule banning bracket classes in apps/roam so this cannot regress; CI already reports new lint findings on changed lines.

Note none of these are user-visible regressions today — the properties simply never applied, and nobody has reported it, which suggests the exact values were not load-bearing.

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Ticket readiness

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Use `Backlog` when the problem is known, the fix is agreed upon, and another engineer can implement it without further product or solution decisions.
- Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but the decision, scope, or solution is not fully settled.
- Keep an explicit Engineering ticket request in Engineering even when it is idea-stage.

## Project selection

Every ticket must use an existing project that is not completed, canceled, archived, or trashed. Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
4. For Obsidian work, use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Confirm the selected project still exists, is active, and includes the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain labels do not block creation. After creation, tell the user when no label was applied or when label selection remained uncertain.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description, status, project, labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

After creation, return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

input.title: Remove inert arbitrary-value Tailwind classes from apps/roam and lint against them
input.project: Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks
input.description:
## Problem

- apps/roam builds no CSS of its own. Its Tailwind classes resolve against Roam's prebuilt `assets/css/tailwind.min.css`, a pre-JIT Tailwind 2 build whose ~6550 rules contain **zero** bracket selectors. Every arbitrary-value class (`text-[13px]`, `min-w-[160px]`, `bg-[#333]`) is therefore inert — the property is simply never applied.
- Nine such call sites exist today. Nothing pushes back on them: `tailwind.config.ts` has `content: []` and is documented as existing only for editor support, so there is no compiler, no purge step, and no lint rule. Editor autocomplete makes it worse by suggesting Tailwind 3 syntax that this build does not contain.
- No user-visible regression is known — the properties never applied and nobody has reported it. The cost is silent dead styling that keeps accruing.

## Solution

- Replace each arbitrary-value class with a catalog utility where one exists. The build is full and unpurged, so every standard Tailwind 2 utility is available.
- For the genuine v2 gaps — `min-w` at a px value, and `font-[inherit]` / `text-[inherit]`, neither of which v2 has utilities for — use a CSS rule instead.
- The hex colors are Blueprint palette values. `apps/roam/AGENTS.md` already says to prefer Blueprint and Roam-native styling over arbitrary colors, so use Blueprint classes rather than reproducing the hex.
- Add an ESLint rule banning bracket classes in apps/roam so this cannot regress.

### Call sites

| File | Classes |
| --- | --- |
| `components/DiscourseNodeMenu.tsx:382` | `border-[#d3d8de]`, `hover:border-[#bfccd6]`, `hover:bg-[#f7f9fc]` |
| `components/settings/DiscourseRelationConfigPanel.tsx:1130` | `font-[inherit]`, `text-[inherit]` |
| `components/settings/PageGroupPanel.tsx:184` | `min-w-[160px]` |
| `components/canvas/CanvasEmbedDialog.tsx:37`, `:41` | `text-[#5c7080]` |
| `components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:84` | `max-h-[240px]`, `min-w-[160px]` |
| `components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:92` | `text-[13px]`, `text-[#333]`, `hover:bg-[#f0f0f0]` |
| `components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx:106` | `bg-[#333]` |

## Done When

- No bracket-syntax Tailwind class remains in `apps/roam/src`.
- Each affected element renders with the intended styling, confirmed against Roam's own stylesheet.

entries.name: mcp__linear-server__save_issue
entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

content.text:
All green. Here's the answer to your question about the tab selection.

## What the two variables actually were

The old code kept **two** pieces of state that were normally identical:

```
activeTabId   // what the user selected — the source of truth
visibleTabId  // what gets displayed — activeTabId, unless it points at a hidden tab
```

`visibleTabId` diverged from `activeTabId` in exactly one case: the selection was one of the two left-sidebar tabs *and* the feature was off. In that case it substituted `homePersonal`.

## Why that substitution was doing real work

I checked Blueprint's source rather than assume, and it's worse than I'd have guessed: **`hidden` is not a Blueprint prop at all.** It falls through `htmlProps` onto the tab title `<div>` as the native HTML `hidden` attribute. Blueprint has no concept of a hidden tab.

Which means the panel rendering ignores it completely. With `renderActiveTabPanelOnly={true}` — which [Settings.tsx:174](apps/roam/src/components/settings/Settings.tsx:174) sets — Blueprint filters panels by `tab.props.id === selectedTabId` and nothing else. So if `selectedTabId` points at a hidden tab you get a broken dialog: the left sidebar panel renders in the body while no tab button is highlighted in the list, because the button it corresponds to is `hidden`. The user sees settings they can't navigate back to.

`visibleTabId` was the thing preventing that. Not decoration.

There's a second, subtler property worth noticing: because it redirected *display* and left `activeTabId` alone, the original target survived. Enable the left sidebar with the dialog still open → `leftSidebarEnabled` flips → the substitution stops applying → the user snaps to the left-sidebar tab they were originally deep-linked to. Resetting `activeTabId` instead would have thrown that away.

## What my change means

Given the current PR's design, nothing. One Left sidebar tab, never hidden, so `visibleTabId` could not differ from `activeTabId` — the guard had no reachable case and deleting it was a genuine no-op.

But that's the point: **the deletion was only valid as a consequence of the design decision Michael is pushing back on.** It wasn't an independent cleanup. The moment you restore feature-gated hiding — which you've said you want — the guard has a live case again and has to come back, because the deep link from the command palette and from [LeftSidebarView.tsx:868](apps/roam/src/components/LeftSidebarView.tsx:868) can still target that tab while the feature is off.

So the two review threads are one decision, not two. Whatever you settle with Michael on where the flag lives, restoring the hiding brings the guard back with it — and if the toggle moves to Admin or Preferences, the guard's fallback should point at *that* tab, not General, so a deep link lands somewhere the user can actually act.

I'd rather not write that code until you've settled the flag's location with him, since the fallback target depends on the answer.

## Also done this turn

- **ENG-2096 cleanup** — you were right, and the consequence was concrete. Main has zero references to the canvas overlay left; our branch still carries the key, schema, accessor mapping, and consumer. Because this PR *re-homes* the panel into `DiscourseContextSettings.tsx`, a file that doesn't exist on main, git would have kept our copy while main's side deleted the key it references — a type error surfacing only at merge. Panel and its import removed; I left the key/schema/consumer alone so main's deletions apply cleanly. Typecheck and 142 tests pass.
- **`grid-cols-[auto_auto]` → flex rows**, and a correction: I told you the grid was rendering as a single column. **That was wrong.** `col-span-2` on the header forces an implicit second column, and implicit columns are auto-sized — which is exactly what `auto auto` would have done. The layout has been correct by accident all along. The class is still dead and the flex version is still the better code, but it's a cleanup, not a bug fix. Both render identically against Roam's real stylesheet (inputs aligned at the same x, same width, vertically centred) — screenshot above.
- **"Saved deep link" comment** reworded to say what's actually true: `SettingsDialog` is exported so outside callers may still pass old ids, and every in-repo call site is updated. Also deleted the "unknown ids pass through" line, which claimed a per-node-tab scheme that doesn't exist.
- **[ENG-2285](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2285/remove-inert-arbitrary-value-tailwind-classes-from-appsroam-and-lint)** filed — nine inert call sites, plus the ESLint rule. Backlog, Roam plugin + Chore, in the Roam assorted tasks project.

CI green on all four pushes. Still open for you: the flag-location decision with Michael, and whether to post my findings on the Tailwind and deep-link threads.

content.text:
All green (each check shows pending then pass across the two pushes).

## The comment you meant

It was a CodeRabbit **nitpick inside a review body**, not an inline thread — which is why it never appeared in my thread sweep. GitHub's `reviewThreads` query only returns inline threads; findings in the review summary itself live in a different place. Worth knowing for future sweeps.

It flagged six components missing explicit return types, `LeftSidebarSettings.tsx:12` among them, against AGENTS.md's "Use explicit return types for functions." Valid — all six are components this PR created or moved. Added `: React.ReactElement` to `SettingsSectionHeading`, `SettingsGroup`, `SettingTitle`, `PreferencesGeneral`, `CanvasSettings`, and `LeftSidebarSettings`. Typecheck, 142 tests, lint clean; pushed.

One other thing in that sweep you may not have registered: Graphite posted a **PR size warning** — over the ~200-line guideline, and it asks for either a split or a written justification in the PR body. Nothing has been added. That's a merge-time nag worth settling.

## Consequences of going back to `visibleTabId`

**It stays coherent, because it lies to Blueprint on purpose.** Passing `visibleTabId` as `selectedTabId` means Blueprint's internal state *is* the fallback tab — so General's title highlights, General's panel renders, and the dialog looks entirely normal. The user never sees a half-state. That's the whole reason it works.

**The divergence is contained but not zero.** `activeTabId` keeps holding the hidden id. Two places feel that:

- The settings snapshot is memoised on it — `useMemo(() => bulkReadSettings(), [activeTabId])`. Harmless here: any later tab click updates `activeTabId` and re-triggers the read.
- The snap-back. If the feature gets enabled while the dialog is open, `leftSidebarTabHidden` flips false, `visibleTabId` falls through to `activeTabId`, and the user is suddenly moved to the Left sidebar tab. Read generously that's the deep link finally being honoured; read plainly it's an unrequested jump. Worth deciding which you want rather than inheriting it.

**Without the guard, restoring hiding is actively broken.** I checked Blueprint's source: `hidden` isn't a Blueprint prop at all, it falls through to the tab title `<div>` as the native HTML attribute. Blueprint has no concept of a hidden tab, and with `renderActiveTabPanelOnly` it filters panels purely on `id === selectedTabId`. So a deep link to a hidden tab renders that panel while its title is `hidden` — nothing in the list is highlighted, and the user is looking at settings with no way back. The guard is the only thing standing between you and that. Keep hiding ⇒ keep the guard, not optional.

**The part that couples to your flag decision.** The fallback target isn't arbitrary — it's the answer to "where do we send someone whose deep link is unreachable?" The old code sent them to `homePersonal`, which was exactly where the enable toggle lived. That's coherent: you land on the tab holding the switch for the thing you were trying to reach. If the flag moves to Admin and the fallback still says Preferences → General, you've landed the user somewhere with no way to enable what they asked for. So:

- Flag → Preferences → General ⇒ fallback is General. One-line restore of the old code.
- Flag → Admin panel ⇒ fallback should be the Admin tab, which is itself conditionally shown (`showAdminPanel`), so the guard needs a second condition — and a non-admin has no reachable destination at all, which pushes you toward the empty-state option instead of a redirect.

That second branch is why I'd still rather not write it until you've settled the location with Michael: it's not the same change in both worlds, and the Admin variant needs a real answer for non-admins.
